sections.title: Naming the reason
sections.content: You already know reklamál ("to complain") from Unit 16, and szeretnék + infinitive for any polite request. Put them together and you have a proper opener: Szeretnék reklamálni. ("I'd like to make a complaint.") reklamál doesn't take an object itself — the reason comes as its own clause, either with mert ("because") or with A probléma az, hogy... ("The problem is that..."), the same hogy-clause pattern you already use with remélem.

sections.title: Opening a complaint
rows: I'd like to make a complaint.

items.spanish: Szeretnék reklamálni, mert nem működik a termék.
items.english: I'd like to complain, because the product doesn't work.

items.spanish: A probléma az, hogy piszkos volt a szoba.
items.english: The problem is that the room was dirty.

sections.content: Lead with Szeretnék reklamálni so the other person knows right away what kind of conversation this is, then explain with mert or A probléma az, hogy... — the same two-step shape works for almost any complaint.
